entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **891. When to start treatment** \[Slider\]: compare strategies like "treat when a marker crosses X" across simulated patients.
entries.title: A marker threshold triggers treatment
entries.lens: the eligibility threshold before comparing dynamic treatment strategies

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **892. The g-formula** \[Slider\]: simulate patient histories under each strategy to estimate its effect.
entries.title: Average outcomes under a strategy
entries.lens: the stipulated history mixture in a g-formula ingredient

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **893. Time-varying weights** \[Slider\]: marginal structural models reweight each period to handle feedback between treatment and health.
entries.title: Weights accumulate across treatment
entries.lens: one time-specific treatment weight before a longitudinal product

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **894. Granger fails with feedback** \[Split\]: two series that cause each other with lags; Granger tests can mislead.
entries.title: Feedback changes a lagged association
entries.lens: the feedback carryover term rather than causal identification by prediction

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **895. Sardines and anchovies** \[Story\]: convergent cross mapping suggested temperature drives both populations, not each other (Sugihara et al., 2012).
entries.title: Two populations share a driver
entries.lens: a common environmental driver in a stipulated structural model

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **896. Impulse responses** \[Slider\]: shock one variable in a time-series model and watch effects ripple through others.
entries.title: A shock propagates through time
entries.lens: the assumed impulse persistence in a scalar linear recurrence

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **897. Crossover carryover** \[Slider\]: a drug's effect lingers into the next period unless a washout gap is added.
entries.title: A previous treatment can carry over
entries.lens: the remaining effect before and after an idealized washout

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **898. Fixed effects** \[Slider\]: per-unit intercepts remove all time-invariant confounders at once.
entries.title: Remove a fixed baseline difference
entries.lens: the time-invariant treated intercept removed by differencing

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **899. Bracketing** \[Split\]: fixed-effects and lagged-outcome models often bound the true effect from opposite sides.
entries.title: Two adjusted estimates can disagree
entries.lens: the estimator endpoints before any bracketing identification claim

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **900. Augmented synthetic control** \[Slider\]: correct a poor pre-period fit with an outcome model.
entries.title: An outcome model changes the baseline
entries.lens: the corrected counterfactual prediction in a synthetic-control illustration

entries.sourceText: - **902. Weights explode** \[Gotcha\]: if the old policy rarely showed an item, one click on it gets an enormous weight.
entries.title: Rare logging actions get large weights
entries.lens: the behavior propensity in a logged-policy reward

entries.sourceText: - **903. Self-normalized IPS** \[Slider\]: normalize the weights and variance drops at the cost of small bias.
entries.title: Normalize an importance-weighted mean
entries.lens: the shared weight scale removed by normalization

entries.sourceText: - **904. Doubly robust OPE** \[Slider\]: combine a reward model with importance weights; either being right is enough.
entries.title: A model plus a weighted residual
entries.lens: the residual correction in a single-action evaluation ingredient

entries.sourceText: - **905. Position bias** \[Slider\]: click rate by rank falls steeply, mostly from attention, not relevance.
entries.title: Position changes click exposure
entries.lens: the examination probability at fixed conditional relevance

entries.sourceText: - **906. Swap the top two** \[Slider\]: randomly swapping adjacent results measures position bias directly (Joachims et al., 2017).
entries.title: A randomized swap reveals click rates
entries.lens: the illustrative position contrast under a stipulated swap design

entries.sourceText: - **907. Counterfactual learning to rank** \[Slider\]: train a ranker on clicks reweighted for position bias.
entries.title: Reweight a click for exposure
entries.lens: the inverse exposure probability on one observed click

entries.sourceText: - **908. Never shown, never clicked** \[Gotcha\]: items the system never exposed look unpopular in its own logs.
entries.title: An unseen item has no logged clicks
entries.lens: the exposure gate before a preference can be observed

entries.sourceText: - **909. Debias popularity** \[Slider\]: reweight by exposure propensity and niche items' true appeal emerges.
entries.title: A niche click may carry more weight
entries.lens: the exposure correction before aggregating popularity

entries.sourceText: - **910. Homogenizing feedback** \[Story\]: simulations show recommender feedback loops make users' consumption more alike (Chaney, Stewart & Engelhardt, 2018).
entries.title: A recommendation loop amplifies a lead
entries.lens: the stipulated feedback strength rather than an empirical homogenization estimate

entries.sourceText: - **911. Would they have bought anyway?** \[Story\]: much of the traffic from recommendations would have reached those products anyway (Sharma, Hofman & Watts, 2015).
entries.title: Incrementality needs a counterfactual
entries.lens: the purchases assumed to occur without recommendations

entries.sourceText: - **913. Whole-slate evaluation** \[Slider\]: estimate a page of recommendations' value without enumerating every combination.
entries.title: A slate probability combines choices
entries.lens: the conditional product in a two-position slate ingredient

entries.sourceText: - **914. Long-term value offline** \[Slider\]: use short-term surrogate signals to estimate retention effects from logs.
entries.title: A short-term signal predicts later value
entries.lens: the supplied surrogate-outcome path under explicit structural assumptions

entries.sourceText: - **915. Simulated users** \[Slider\]: test a recommender against synthetic users with known preferences before launch.
entries.title: Known preferences benchmark a policy
entries.lens: the reward heterogeneity of two synthetic user types

entries.sourceText: - **916. Log with exploration** \[Slider\]: a little randomness in production makes future offline evaluation possible.
entries.title: Exploration creates logging support
entries.lens: the positive behavior propensity needed for finite importance weighting

entries.sourceText: - **917. Ratings aren't random** \[Gotcha\]: on randomly assigned songs, users' ratings were far lower than on songs they chose to rate (Marlin & Zemel, 2009).
entries.title: Chosen ratings select favorable cases
entries.lens: the outcome-dependent response propensity in a ratings illustration

entries.sourceText: - **918. Relevance vs diversity** \[Slider\]: slide toward diversity and watch accuracy and coverage trade off.
entries.title: A relevance-diversity score has weights
entries.lens: the explicit scoring tradeoff rather than a guaranteed accuracy gain

entries.sourceText: - **919. Fair exposure** \[Slider\]: allocate ranking attention in proportion to merit, not just to the top item.
entries.title: Allocate exposure toward a target
entries.lens: the exposure share needed to match a stipulated merit target

entries.sourceText: - **920. Judge vs A/B** \[Measure\]: predict which of two ranker changes wins an A/B test, then compare your calls with an LLM judge's.
entries.title: Judge confidence meets experiment wins
entries.lens: a descriptive agreement count rather than a validated LLM judge

entries.sourceText: - **921. SIR curves** \[Slider\]: set the reproduction number and watch susceptible, infected and recovered curves cross.
entries.title: Take one epidemic state step
entries.lens: the transmission term in a normalized SIR update

entries.sourceText: - **922. Flatten the curve** \[Slider\]: reduce contacts and the infection peak drops below hospital capacity.
entries.title: Fewer contacts slow an infected stock
entries.lens: the contact-rate parameter before computing a complete epidemic peak

entries.sourceText: - **923. Herd immunity threshold** \[Slider\]: the share immune needed is 1 − 1/R₀; at R₀ = 3, about 67%.
entries.title: Immunity changes reproduction
entries.lens: the homogeneous perfect-immunity threshold

entries.sourceText: - **924. Overshoot** \[Gotcha\]: an unchecked epidemic infects far more people than the herd-immunity threshold.
entries.title: A threshold is not a final case count
entries.lens: the critical immune share rather than epidemic overshoot

entries.sourceText: - **925. Superspreading** \[Slider\]: lower the dispersion parameter and a small share of cases cause most transmission.
entries.title: Offspring variance changes total spread
entries.lens: the offspring-size variance in a compound transmission count

entries.sourceText: - **927. Small worlds** \[Slider\]: add a few long-range links to a neighborhood network and spread accelerates sharply.
entries.title: Connectivity can support broad reach
entries.lens: the mean-degree threshold in a random-graph reachability model

entries.sourceText: - **928. Vaccinate the hubs** \[Slider\]: targeting highly connected people beats random vaccination.
entries.title: A hub holds more contact exposure
entries.lens: the degree-weighted contact share before a vaccination policy comparison

entries.sourceText: - **929. Trace backward** \[Gotcha\]: finding who infected a case uncovers more infections than tracing whom the case infected.
entries.title: Tracing back oversamples prolific cases
entries.lens: the size bias from following a random transmission link

entries.sourceText: - **931. Complex contagion** \[Slider\]: behaviors that need several exposures spread better through clustered networks (Centola, 2010).
entries.title: A behavior waits for enough exposure
entries.lens: the minimum-exposure threshold in a binary activation ingredient

entries.sourceText: - **932. Information cascade** \[Measure\]: guess an urn's color after seeing earlier guesses; soon everyone just follows the crowd.
entries.title: Public guesses can update private odds
entries.lens: the supplied social likelihood message under an independence assumption

entries.sourceText: - **933. Viral cascade sizes** \[Slider\]: most posts barely spread; a few explode, a heavy-tailed distribution.
entries.title: Many cascades end early
entries.lens: the offspring law in a finite branching cascade

entries.sourceText: - **934. Riot thresholds** \[Slider\]: change one person's threshold and a crowd goes from calm to riot (Granovetter, 1978).
entries.title: One threshold can change activation
entries.lens: the threshold crossing before a full crowd cascade

entries.sourceText: - **935. Rumors** \[Slider\]: spreaders stop once they meet people who already know; part of the population never hears.
entries.title: A spreader can leave the active state
entries.lens: the stipulated transition out of active spreading

entries.sourceText: - **936. Doubling time** \[Slider\]: convert a daily growth rate into doubling time; 7% a day doubles in about 10 days.
entries.title: Turn growth into a doubling time
entries.lens: the discrete daily growth assumption

entries.sourceText: - **937. Nowcasting** \[Slider\]: recent cases are undercounted due to reporting delays; correct the curve's tail.
entries.title: Correct an incomplete reporting tail
entries.lens: the reporting-completion probability in one nowcast correction

entries.sourceText: - **938. Case vs infection fatality** \[Gotcha\]: dividing deaths by confirmed cases overstates fatality when many infections go uncounted.
entries.title: Confirmed cases change a fatality ratio
entries.lens: the ascertainment denominator rather than a clinical risk estimate

entries.sourceText: - **939. Incubation period** \[Slider\]: add an exposed-but-not-infectious stage and the epidemic slows and stretches.
entries.title: A waiting stage delays infectiousness
entries.lens: a stipulated incubation time before a full SEIR trajectory

entries.sourceText: - **940. Wastewater signals** \[Story\]: sewage sampling tracked COVID trends in cities, often ahead of case counts.
entries.title: An early signal precedes a case count
entries.lens: the supplied lead-signal contribution in a surveillance illustration

entries.sourceText: - **941. Draw with circles** \[Slider\]: trace any shape with your finger; a chain of rotating circles (epicycles) redraws it, sharper with each added circle.
entries.title: Add two rotating vectors
entries.lens: the higher harmonic in a finite epicycle trace

entries.sourceText: - **942. Square wave from sines** \[Slider\]: add odd harmonics one by one; the overshoot at the corners never fully goes away (Gibbs phenomenon).
entries.title: Odd harmonics sharpen a square wave
entries.lens: the truncation order of a square-wave Fourier series

entries.sourceText: - **943. Whistle a spectrum** \[Measure\]: whistle into the phone and watch a single sharp peak in the live spectrum.
entries.title: A pure tone has one frequency
entries.lens: the frequency of a synthesized waveform without microphone capture

entries.sourceText: - **944. Your voice spectrogram** \[Measure\]: say vowels and watch their distinct frequency bands light up.
entries.title: A voice component changes frequency
entries.lens: one illustrative sinusoidal component before a voice spectrogram

entries.sourceText: - **945. Wagon-wheel effect** \[Slider\]: spin a wheel past the camera's frame rate and it appears to turn backward.
entries.title: A sampled rotation can reverse
entries.lens: the principal signed alias at a fixed frame rate

entries.sourceText: - **947. Colors of noise** \[Split\]: listen to white, pink and brown noise and see their spectra slope differently.
entries.title: Noise colors have different slopes
entries.lens: the frequency exponent of a stipulated power spectrum

entries.sourceText: - **948. Hidden rhythm** \[Slider\]: a periodogram finds a weekly cycle buried in very noisy daily data.
entries.title: A periodic component has a timescale
entries.lens: the specified frequency before a periodogram estimation

entries.sourceText: - **949. Sunspots** \[Story\]: the spectrum of centuries of sunspot counts shows a strong peak near 11 years.
entries.title: A long cycle has a low frequency
entries.lens: a stipulated cycle frequency without a sunspot-data fit

entries.sourceText: - **950. Image frequencies** \[Slider\]: keep low frequencies for blur, high frequencies for edges, all in the Fourier domain.
entries.title: Blur suppresses high frequencies
entries.lens: the Gaussian transfer function at a chosen spatial frequency

entries.sourceText: - **951. JPEG** \[Slider\]: discard high-frequency DCT coefficients and watch file size drop and blocks appear.
entries.title: Removing detail attenuates coefficients
entries.lens: a frequency attenuation ingredient rather than a JPEG implementation

entries.sourceText: - **952. Convolution theorem** \[Slider\]: blurring in space is multiplying in frequency; watch both views update together.
entries.title: Convolution becomes a frequency gain
entries.lens: the Gaussian convolution multiplier across frequencies

entries.sourceText: - **954. Spectrum of a random process** \[Slider\]: an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process has a smooth spectrum whose bend moves with its mean-reversion speed.
entries.title: Reversion sets a spectral bend
entries.lens: the reversion rate in a stationary OU spectrum

entries.sourceText: - **955. Autocorrelation ↔ spectrum** \[Slider\]: change a process's autocorrelation and its power spectrum changes in lockstep (Wiener–Khinchin).
entries.title: Correlation changes spectral power
entries.lens: the AR coefficient linking autocovariance and spectrum

entries.sourceText: - **956. Random Fourier features** \[Slider\]: sum random cosine waves to approximate a Gaussian-process kernel; more features, better fit.
entries.title: One Fourier feature contributes a wave
entries.lens: the sampled angular frequency before kernel averaging

entries.sourceText: - **957. Why sums become bells** \[Slider\]: adding random variables multiplies their Fourier transforms, which squeezes them toward a Gaussian.
entries.title: Products of transforms approach a bell
entries.lens: the standardized independent coin-sum characteristic function

entries.sourceText: - **958. No cycles in returns** \[Gotcha\]: the spectrum of daily stock returns is nearly flat; "market cycles" mostly vanish.
entries.title: Uncorrelated increments have flat power
entries.lens: the frequency-invariant spectrum of a stipulated white process

entries.sourceText: - **959. Song fingerprints** \[Story\]: music recognition apps match constellations of spectrogram peaks against a database.
entries.title: A fingerprint begins with frequencies
entries.lens: one component before a spectrogram-peak matching system

entries.sourceText: - **960. Fourier denoising** \[Slider\]: zero out frequencies with little power and a noisy signal comes back clean.
entries.title: A low-pass filter removes detail
entries.lens: the attenuation of high-frequency signal and noise together

entries.sourceText: - **962. Perlin landscapes** \[Slider\]: layer noise octaves to build game-style terrain and clouds.
entries.title: A second octave adds finer variation
entries.lens: the higher-frequency component in a terrain ingredient

entries.sourceText: - **963. Hurst exponent** \[Slider\]: fractional Brownian motion goes from rough to smooth as the exponent rises.
entries.title: The Hurst exponent changes scaling
entries.lens: the Gaussian increment scale at a fixed distance

entries.sourceText: - **964. How long is a coastline?** \[Gotcha\]: measure with a shorter ruler and the coastline gets longer, without limit.
entries.title: A shorter ruler measures more length
entries.lens: the idealized fractal measurement scale

entries.sourceText: - **965. Growing snowflakes** \[Slider\]: random walkers stick on contact and grow branching, coral-like clusters.
entries.title: A walker reaches a growth boundary
entries.lens: the one-dimensional hitting ingredient before aggregation

entries.sourceText: - **966. Turing patterns** \[Slider\]: noise plus reaction and diffusion produces spots and stripes like animal coats.
entries.title: A perturbation can grow or decay
entries.lens: one linearized mode before a reaction-diffusion pattern

entries.sourceText: - **967. Percolation clusters** \[Slider\]: color connected clusters as density crosses the threshold; one giant cluster suddenly spans the grid.
entries.title: A connected component emerges
entries.lens: the random-graph connectivity ingredient rather than a lattice simulation

entries.sourceText: - **968. Critical slowing** \[Slider\]: near the Ising model's critical temperature, domains of all sizes appear and change very slowly.
entries.title: Slow change reduces independent samples
entries.lens: the autocorrelation cost in a critical-slowing illustration

entries.sourceText: - **969. Random parking** \[Predict\]: cars park at random spots on a curb; they fill only about 75% of it before no gap fits.
entries.title: A parking realization leaves gaps
entries.lens: the occupied length in two stipulated parking outcomes

entries.sourceText: - **970. Random packing** \[Predict\]: shaken spheres fill about 64% of space, below the 74% of perfect stacking.
entries.title: Packing fraction depends on geometry
entries.lens: the occupied volume in two supplied packing illustrations

entries.sourceText: - **972. Uncertainty maps** \[Slider\]: kriging maps both the estimate and where it's unreliable, far from sensors.
entries.title: Uncertainty grows away from a sensor
entries.lens: the one-observation Gaussian-process posterior variance

entries.sourceText: - **973. Smoothed crime map** \[Slider\]: Bayesian smoothing calms the noisy rates of small neighborhoods.
entries.title: Small areas shrink toward a prior
entries.lens: the sampling uncertainty in a toy area-rate estimate

entries.sourceText: - **974. Arctic circle** \[Slider\]: random domino tilings of an Aztec diamond freeze into order outside a circle and stay chaotic inside.
entries.title: Local tile order changes entropy
entries.lens: a binary orientation uncertainty rather than an Aztec-diamond sampler

entries.sourceText: - **975. Random mazes** \[Slider\]: a random spanning tree on a grid becomes a perfect maze.
entries.title: A tree has one fewer edge than nodes
entries.lens: the connected-tree edge count before generating a random maze

entries.sourceText: - **976. Cosmic web vs random** \[Split\]: real galaxy maps show filaments and voids; a Poisson scatter doesn't.
entries.title: A random baseline has empty regions
entries.lens: the void probability under a homogeneous Poisson baseline

entries.sourceText: - **977. Noisy cellular automata** \[Slider\]: add randomness to simple local rules and watch fire, growth or traffic patterns.
entries.title: A random rule thins active events
entries.lens: the independent activation probability before a cellular automaton

entries.sourceText: - **978. Self-avoiding walk** \[Slider\]: a random walk that can't cross itself spreads faster, like a polymer chain.
entries.title: Independent steps set a walk scale
entries.lens: the unrestricted-walk benchmark before self-avoidance

entries.sourceText: - **979. Semicircle law** \[Slider\]: eigenvalues of a large random symmetric matrix pile up in a semicircle.
entries.title: A random-matrix limit has a shape
entries.lens: the limiting semicircle density at two coordinates

entries.sourceText: - **980. Texture synthesis** \[Slider\]: grow a new texture pixel by pixel by sampling matching neighborhoods from an example (Efros & Leung, 1999).
entries.title: A neighborhood affects a texture bit
entries.lens: one local conditional before example-based texture synthesis

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **981. Itô's correction** \[Slider\]: the average growth of a volatile asset falls below its expected return by half the variance.
entries.title: Volatility subtracts from log growth
entries.lens: the quadratic-variation correction in a geometric diffusion

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **982. Black–Scholes** \[Slider\]: drag volatility, time and strike and watch an option's price surface bend.
entries.title: A toy call responds to volatility
entries.lens: the constant volatility in a no-dividend European option model

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **983. Price an option by simulation** \[Slider\]: simulate thousands of price paths and average the payoffs.
entries.title: Average option payoffs after the kink
entries.lens: the payoff convexity in a two-outcome pricing benchmark

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **984. The volatility smile** \[Gotcha\]: real option prices imply different volatilities by strike, because real tails are fatter than the model's.
entries.title: An assumed smile changes model prices
entries.lens: two supplied strike-specific volatilities rather than a market calibration

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **985. Diffusion from random walkers** \[Slider\]: thousands of random walkers spread into the bell-shaped heat equation solution.
entries.title: Walkers spread into a heat kernel
entries.lens: the elapsed diffusion time in a continuum limit

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **986. Escaping a well** \[Slider\]: a noisy particle eventually hops over an energy barrier; escape time grows exponentially with barrier height.
entries.title: A barrier makes escape much slower
entries.lens: the exponential barrier-to-noise ratio with unit prefactor

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **987. Stochastic resonance** \[Slider\]: adding the right amount of noise helps a threshold detector catch a weak signal.
entries.title: Noise changes a threshold estimate
entries.lens: the Gaussian observation-noise ingredient before stochastic resonance

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **989. Noisy predators and prey** \[Slider\]: random fluctuations push cycling populations to extinction.
entries.title: A population can reach extinction
entries.lens: the offspring distribution in a bounded extinction model

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **990. Spiking neurons** \[Slider\]: an integrate-and-fire neuron turns noisy input into a train of spikes.
entries.title: A neuron fires after a threshold
entries.lens: the threshold crossing before integrate-and-fire reset dynamics

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **991. Half-life from chaos** \[Predict\]: each atom decays at random, yet the population halves on schedule.
entries.title: Random atoms have a smooth mean decay
entries.lens: the elapsed half-lives of independent decays

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **992. Molecular speeds** \[Slider\]: random collisions settle into the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution.
entries.title: Three velocity components give a speed
entries.lens: the speed coordinate in a Maxwell distribution

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **993. Gas spreading** \[Slider\]: open a divider; particles spread and almost never return to one side.
entries.title: A gas rarely returns to one side
entries.lens: the independent equilibrium occupancy of every particle

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **994. Order book** \[Slider\]: random buy and sell orders arrive and the price emerges from their matches.
entries.title: Orders change a displayed imbalance
entries.lens: the submitted buy-minus-sell count before order-book matching

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **995. Interest-rate paths** \[Slider\]: a mean-reverting Vasicek model fans out possible future rates.
entries.title: A rate returns toward its center
entries.lens: the conditional mean of a stipulated Vasicek-type rate

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **996. Brownian ratchet** \[Slider\]: an asymmetric, switching potential turns random jiggling into directed motion, like molecular motors.
entries.title: Asymmetric transitions create a drift
entries.lens: the supplied directional transition difference before a ratchet model

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **998. The coalescent** \[Slider\]: trace sampled genes backward in time as their lineages merge into a family tree.
entries.title: More lineages merge sooner
entries.lens: the pair count determining a neutral coalescent waiting time

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **999. Folding landscape** \[Slider\]: a protein chain explores an energy landscape with Monte Carlo moves, finding its folded shape.
entries.title: A proposed fold has an energy ratio
entries.lens: the Metropolis acceptance ingredient for a quadratic toy energy

entries.sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
entries.sourceText: - **1000. The jackpot experiment** \[Story\]: highly variable mutant counts across bacterial cultures showed mutations arise at random before selection, not in response to it (Luria & Delbrück, 1943).
entries.title: Early jackpots inflate count variance
entries.lens: the clone-size variance in a compound mutation-count illustration
